title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-08-19
lineage: Master/1st generation cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon > Digital Audio Labs Card Deluxe soundcard (96Mhz/24 bit)> HD
source: Master Audience Cassette; Sony TC-124 with Sony Stereo Mic

ai_review.summary: A joyous acoustic‑first show captured on an audience tape with good enough sound to enjoy the historic first performances.
ai_review.review: The August 19 1970 Fillmore West set is prized for its historic moments – the debut of Ripple, Brokedown Palace, Operator and Truckin’ – and a soaring acoustic segment that many reviewers call “motherlovin' wonderful.”  The audience recording isn’t pristine, but it’s clear enough to hear Pig’s surprise piano work and the band’s loose‑but‑fun vibe; a few fans note it’s a bit sloppy and recommend a later Jones‑Minches mix for superior fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical significance with several first‑time songs and an engaging acoustic set outweighs modest recording imperfections; most reviewers rate 4–5 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Variable sound quality – some describe it as “great,” others note it’s not the best version available.  The tape captures the acoustic piano (Pig) and overall ambience, though a few listeners find it a bit sloppy and recommend an alternate Jones‑Minches source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic first set that builds excitement, followed by a classic electric second half; the show feels loose but joyful, with historic debuts punctuating the flow.

band_member_comments.Keys: Pig (Ron "Pig" McKernan) is heard on acoustic piano during the set, surprising many listeners.
